On Saturday, 30 January 2021 at 16:33:07 UTC murray...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi Richard
> It's a bug, of course. Thanks for your detailed report. I have fixed it in the pre-release version available here secr_4.3.4.zip <https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/zip/secr_4.3.4.zip> (Windows binary) or here secr_4.3.4.tar.gz <https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/zip/secr_4.3.4.tar.gz> (source).
> As a workaround, you can also read data as if from a "proximity" detector and then convert to "multi":
> traps<- make.grid(detector = "proximity")
> chp <- make.capthist(captures, traps)
> chm <- reduce(chp, outputdetector = "multi", dropunused = FALSE)
> The result is not identical but the differences are subtle and I think ignorable.
> Murray
>
> On Saturday, January 30, 2021 at 1:15:48 PM UTC+13 Richard Glennie wrote:
> > Hello all,
> >
> > Just wanted to query whether this is a possible bug in secr 4.3.3 or I am misunderstanding something.

> > I found some unusual behaviour when using make.capthist with multi detectors. It reported a warning that it was "dropping repeat detections within occasions at exclusive detectors (traps)" when I was sure I had removed all such repeat detections.
> >
> > Find attached a script that reproduces the problem for a minimal example and proposes where I think the problem is in make.capthist.
> >
> > Best,
> >
> > Richard

Marie

On Thursday, January 28, 2021 at 11:15:41 PM UTC murray...@gmail.com wrote:
> I think you can interpret P as the probability of observing a value that large under the null hypothesis that the data were generated under the fitted model. So small P (<0.05?) implies significant lack of fit. There is no canned measure of overdispersion. Goodness-of-fit and overdispersion have yet to be fully investigated for SECR models: I'm not claiming expertise here, just providing a tool.
> Murray
>

> >
> > I would like to check overdispersion of my dataset vs my top-ranked model. I have looked up several times the secr manual and the different threads of this group related to the topic, but I am still unsure about it, so I am turning to you for guidance.
> >
> > From what I understood, I would need to run a goodness of fit test on my top-ranked model using secr.test and the statfn function given in the example, i.e:
> > bothfn <- function(object)
> >                 { CH <- object$capthist
> >                 f1 <- sum(apply(abs(CH) > 0, 1, sum) == 1) / nrow(CH)

> >                 }

> > f1            0.65
> > devdf      0.60
> >
> > Which means that the rank of the observed value in the vector combining the observed value and simulated values is 12. This is where I get stuck. How do you link these probabilities to goodness of fit and overdispersion? The greater P(devdf ), the better the fit?

> > Apologies if my question seems obvious.
> >
> > Best wishes
> >
> > Marie

messages.body_plain:
Dear Colleagues

Apologies for cross-posting and for this non-modelling related message. Please feel free to pass this on to anyone you think might be considering a MSc and has interests in statistical ecology.

We are very pleased to announce that we are taking applications for the second intake of our new MSc in Statistical Ecology detailed in the attached leaflet. This year there are two fee-waiver scholarships available, which can be applied for when applying for admission to the MSc.

The MSc aims to give students
a sound understanding of the statistical foundations of modern methods in statistical ecology
Knowledge and skills to use these methods effectively
experience of applying them to real-world problems, under the supervision of experts, some of whom are leading researchers in this field

The Programme involves two semesters of taught courses and a 3-month summer research dissertation. It is taught by staff at the interdisciplinary Centre for Research into Ecological and Environmental Modelling (https://www.creem.st-andrews.ac.uk/). The summer dissertation includes optional placements with collaborators in the UK or abroad, to give students experience of dealing with real-world problems in statistical ecology.

We are delighted to announce that we intend to award scholarships to partially or fully cover MSc fees to selected successful applicants.

messages.subject: Telemetry Scale and Integration
messages.body_plain:
Hi Everyone,

I have successfully input telemetry data into my secr density models using MS.capthist(captrap, telem). The standard addTelemetry(captrap, telem, type = "concurrent", collapsetelemetry = TRUE) produced NA estimates. My study is only 1 session so it seems like the MS.capthist function should still be appropriate for my data, but is ‘independent’ the only option when using MS.capthist? I would like to have the telemetry data as ‘concurrent’ if possible.

Secondly, I needed to scale my telemetry 1e6 to get the data to integrate correctly. I have figured out how to scale my capture history data by 1e6, but when I have attempted to scale my masks/mask covariates by 1e6 the models no longer run. Is there code equivalent to telemetryscale for masks that I am missing? Is there a better way to scale masks other than manually dividing the coordinates?

Thank you,

 Katherine Kurth

messages.subject: Model average of multisession and density with habitat covariates
messages.subject_clean: Model average of multisession and density with habitat covariates
messages.body_plain:
HI all

I am seeking some advice. We have several camera trap surveys of two months each, from which we identified different carnivore species and these were set at different regions of a protected area, over a period of 6 years

Here is a summary of the data for one of the species:
                   data2 data3 data4 data5
Occasions        95      468      659     1554
Detections      151       88       53       82
Animals          58       32       23       25
Detectors        81       41       51       78

 data2 data3 data4 data5
 "F"      "F"      "F"      "F"
 "M"      "M"      "M"      "M"

After being able to model each survey/year independently as the data came in, we now want to calculate densities of each species over the whole park (the mask is the park with added habitat covariates), by using a multi-session approach (year = session) and letting density vary by session and g0 and sigma vary by sex.
Will the model average over the multi-session outputs give the intended overall density result? Will we be able to predictDsurface on the average model? We are able to obtain for each session reliable estimates with the following model structure:
lapply(data,secr.fit, model=list(D~Session,g0~h2,sigma~h2),mask=MASK, hcov="Sex",trace = FALSE,method = 'Nelder-Mead')

But we keep failing when we start to add the habitat covariates (Vegetation, Water...) to the density model and we keep getting the Error: vector memory exhausted (limit reached?)

Any insight is most welcomed, thank you

Rafael

messages.subject: Problem when constructing multi-session object
messages.body_plain:
Dear SECR users,

I am estimating the densities of stream-dwelling newts at three locations (i.e. stream segments) in Pyrenees mountains, using secr 4.3.3 and more specifically using secrlinear package. The three locations are spatially independant and I thus want to fit multiple session models to try to detect variations in estimated parameters between sites.

I have 4 or 5 occasions per session, all realized during the activity period of the species. Each session has its own detector layout.
When constructing a multi-session object with read.capthist, I get an error message saying 'failed to match some capture locations to detector site', whereas I double checked all capture and trap locations. This error does not occur when constructing single-session objects, one for each location.
I also tryied to construc multi-session object with only two of the three locations, and the error message always occur when there is the location N°3 in the object. Thus it appears that the problem comes from only one session, but I don't understand why. I tried to change the names of the detector but without any success..

Is the number of occasions per session supposed to be the same for each session?

Here is my code to illustrate the process and my data attached (capthist + trap file which poses a problem).

# INPUT DIRECTORY
inputdir <-  "C:/myDirectory"
captfile2019_multi_tous <- paste0(inputdir, "/capthist_fougaxsalaucassrats_2019.txt")

# TRAP FILES (one for each session)
fougaxtrap <- paste0(inputdir, "/fougaxtrap.txt")
salautrap <- paste0(inputdir, "/salautrap_XY.txt")
cassratstrap <- paste0(inputdir, "/cassratstrap_XY.txt")

# CONSTRUCTION OF CAPTURE-HISTORY
casper2019_multi <- read.capthist(captfile2019_multi_tous, trapfile = list(fougaxtrap, salautrap, cassratstrap), covname = "Sex", detector = "multi") # maybe something wrong here ?
Error in make.capthist(captures = capturelist[[i]], traps = trps, fmt = fmt, : failed to match some capture locations to detector sites

Thanks in advance for help !
Manon

messages.subject: Re: Model average of multisession and density with habitat covariates, or what you are trying to do.
messages.subject_clean: Model average of multisession and density with habitat covariates, or what you are trying to do.
messages.body_plain:
Rafael
I can't quite follow how your surveys relate to years and sessions.
1. Can we assume you are analysing species separately?
2. I take it you don't want to model temporal variation, rather to assume no temporal variation and focus on space?
3. Something must be wrong for you to have 1554 occasions in two months.
4. Are you really interested in averaging over models (which models?)? Or just getting an average density across years and covariates?
5. I haven't thought about model-averaging the predicted density surface - it's possible in principle, but you might have to compute it yourself.
6. I can't see where the memory problem comes from. Although you attribute it to including habitat covariates of density, that may merely be the straw that broke the camel's back. It's not surprising you run out of memory if the number of occasions is artficially inflated. Also, you can fit models using a mask that discards pixels distant from any detector, and later extrapolate that model to a much larger mask for the whole park.
Murray

messages.body_plain:
That helps. If I'm understanding your design right, it seems time and space are confounded - you might argue that one or the other is unimportant, but I don't think you can have both without a more rigorous (randomized) design.
If each survey is a 'session' in 'secr' then you can model the session differences with a session covariate (possibly grouping similar times or habitats). (If the covariate is a factor then it can be coded with a mean effect as described in a different context here section 7.8 <https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/openCR-vignette.pdf>). If you go the other route of fitting spatial covariates of density then, yes, I think you can use predictDsurface, but the details will depend on your model.

On (6) I meant 'can' i.e. you can fit a model efficiently with a restricted mask and extrapolate later with a larger mask.
Murray

Hi everyone,

I'm currently following the "A tutorial on fitting spatially explicit capture–recapture models in secr " document but I keep getting an error message when trying to estimate sigma.

This is where I get up to:
library(secr)
setwd("C:/Users/lmcra/OneDrive/Desktop/Career/Uni/Honours/Data/Combined")

summary(PossumCH)
par(mar = c(1,1,3,1))

Does anyone know how to get passed this error?

Cheers,
Lachlan McRae

messages.body_plain:
Sorry, I didn't realize it was an argument value of the cat() function.

So I ran a reprex and it worked for me without error:

library(secr)
dbar(captdata)
initialsigma <- RPSV(captdata, CC = TRUE)

cat("Quick and biased estimate of sigma =", initialsigma, "m\n")

So I suspect something is wrong with the initialsigma value on your end. It should be a single value after you ran the RPSV() function. However, the error suggests that the value you inputted is a list rather than a value. So make sure you're running an unlisted version of your capthist in the RPSV function.
